tasks.short: Explain injury prevention in sessions, answer e-mailed questions from vetted texts, write articles, give workshops and publish articles.

steps.what: Physical therapist explains injury prevention and ergonomics to patients in sessions
Physical therapist writes replies to e-mailed questions from the public about physical therapy

loop.input: An e-mailed question and the practice's approved leaflets plus vetted, guideline-based public health texts.
loop.output: A draft reply that quotes the matching passages, each with its source link.
loop.check: Code checks every quoted passage matches its source word for word and that the reply gives no personal diagnosis or treatment; the therapist reads each quote to see that it supports the answer and fits the question asked; questions about a person's own complaint get a standard invitation to book a visit, and unclear cases are written by hand.
loop.stop: One draft per question; no matching passage means the therapist writes the reply.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions come in free text on many topics; a fixed FAQ does not match them.

steps.what: Physical therapist checks the final reply: it answers the question, quotes support each statement, it gives no personal treatment advice, and it goes to the person who asked
Physical therapist sends the checked reply
Physical therapist writes educational articles for the practice website
Physical therapist gives ergonomics workshops at companies and sports clubs
Physical therapist checks the final article: facts and advice match the sources, no patient details, and the right page on the website
Physical therapist publishes the checked article: uploaded and formatted by hand today, by one release to the website in the house layout after the change

tasks.design: For e-mailed questions, a bounded step drafts a reply that quotes the practice's approved leaflets and vetted public health texts, and the therapist edits, checks and sends it; personal complaints get an invitation to book. Finished articles are saved in the shared document space ({DOCS}) and the website ({CMS}) publishes them in the house layout once the therapist checks and releases them. Teaching in sessions, writing articles and workshops stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every e-mail was written from scratch and articles were formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted, guideline-based public texts exist, and language models can match free text to them.
tasks.still_hard: General advice must not turn into treatment advice without an exam.
tasks.human_edge: Showing an office team how they actually sit, not how a poster says.
tasks.altitude: The therapist edits drafted replies instead of writing every one.

reach.learn: Whether quoted replies can be sent after a therapist's check.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts offers guideline-based patient information written with GP and specialist associations and the patient federation.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: assess risks, test and monitor.

assumptions: Boundary: from questions and topics to answers, articles and workshops; individual treatment is outside.
Input contract: approved leaflets kept by the practice's therapists; public texts used under their terms; fallback is writing from scratch.
Teaching, articles and workshops do not change.
No chatbot answers the public.
s2 keeps 55 for reading each draft and its quotes; the check (s2b) and send (s2c) take 1 each. s5 keeps 10 for the release; formatting goes.
research_questions: How many questions match a vetted passage?

already_counted.description: Physical therapist edits each drafted reply.

incremental.description: Physical therapist keeps the approved leaflets current.

approvals.approved_version: The article text and images exactly as checked by the therapist in s3b, published once on the practice website; any change needs a new check.
The reply exactly as checked by the therapist in s2b, sent once to the person who asked; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few questions fit the approved leaflets, so most replies are written by hand and s2 keeps 80 (7.6); high: leaflets cover most questions (12.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recognise findings outside physical therapy, explain them, write and send the referral and phone the GP when urgent.

steps.what: Physical therapist recognises findings outside physical therapy during the exam
Physical therapist informs patients about the findings and the need to see another practitioner
Physical therapist writes the referral letter to the GP
Physical therapist checks the final referral: findings and reason match the exam, the urgency is right, and it goes to the patient's GP
Physical therapist sends the checked referral: by fax or post today, by one release through secure care messaging after the change
Physical therapist phones the GP about urgent findings

tasks.design: A referral template in the practice record ({OTHER}) fills patient details, history, test results and the therapist's findings; the therapist completes and checks it and then releases it by secure care messaging. Recognising findings, informing the patient and urgent calls stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Referral letters were typed and faxed or posted.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice records fill referral templates and send them by secure care messaging.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a patient something may be serious takes care and time.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining calmly why a patient should see the GP today.

reach.learn: Whether structured referrals speed up follow-up.

evidence.claim: Practice records fill referral templates and send them by secure care messaging.
Solely automated care decisions need a legal basis under GDPR article 22(2); the therapist decides every referral.

assumptions: Boundary: from findings to the referral sent; the GP's follow-up is outside.
Input contract: exam data recorded by the therapist; template set by the practice's therapists; fallback is typing and posting.
Recognising, informing and urgent calls do not change.
GP time is outside the therapist's savings.
s3 keeps 60: details, history and test results fill from the record, but the reason for referral and the concern are written by the therapist. s4 keeps 10 for the release.
research_questions: Do referred patients see the GP sooner?

already_counted.description: Physical therapist checks and completes the filled template.

incremental.description: No new work: learning the template is a one-off; completing it is inside s3.

approvals.approved_version: The referral letter exactly as checked by the therapist in s3b, sent once by secure care messaging to the patient's GP; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the template fits few red-flag cases, so s3 keeps 80, and many GPs still need post, so s4 keeps 50 (8.8); high: template and secure messaging as designed (16.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review goals and scores, discuss discharge, write and send the discharge report, close the episode and book follow-up care.

steps.what: Physical therapist reviews whether goals and projected outcomes have been attained
Physical therapist discusses discharge and self-management with the patient
Physical therapist writes the discharge report with outcomes and follow-up advice
Physical therapist checks the final discharge report: outcomes and advice match the record and what was agreed with the patient, and it goes to the referring GP
Physical therapist sends the checked discharge report: by e-mail today, by one release through secure care messaging after the change
Physical therapist closes the treatment episode: codes chosen by hand today; after the change the therapist checks the billing codes the record sets and closes it
Physical therapist books follow-up care or referrals where needed

tasks.design: A discharge template in the practice record ({OTHER}) fills goals, outcome scores over time and the number of sessions, and the therapist adds the follow-up advice and checks it. The therapist releases the checked report to the GP by secure care messaging, then checks the billing codes the record sets and closes the episode. Deciding on discharge, the talk with the patient and booking follow-up stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Discharge reports were typed and episodes closed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice records fill report templates from scores and close episodes by rule.
tasks.still_hard: Some patients want to continue when goals are met; the talk takes time.
tasks.human_edge: Giving a patient confidence to manage without the therapist.

reach.learn: Whether rule-closed episodes cut billing errors.

evidence.claim: Practice records fill report templates from outcome scores and close episodes by rule.
The patient dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the discharge review to follow-up booked; later visits are outside.
Input contract: outcome scores and goals recorded in the record; billing rules set by the practice administrator; fallback is typing.
Deciding, talking and booking do not change.
GP time is outside the therapist's savings.
s3 keeps 60: goals, scores and sessions fill from the record, but the follow-up advice is written by the therapist. s4 keeps 10 for the release; s5 keeps 10 for checking codes and closing.
research_questions: Do discharge reports reach GPs within a week?

already_counted.description: Physical therapist checks the filled discharge report.

incremental.description: No new work: checking the billing codes is inside s5.

approvals.approved_version: The discharge report exactly as checked by the therapist in s3b, sent once by secure care messaging to the referring GP; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: scores are often missing from the record, so s3 keeps 80, and many GPs still need e-mail, so s4 keeps 50 (17.8); high: template and secure messaging as designed (25.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate fit and gait, adjust the device, discuss modifications with the orthotist, write and send the request and record the outcome.

steps.what: Physical therapist evaluates the fit of prosthetic or orthotic devices and the patient's gait
Physical therapist adjusts straps, padding and settings
Physical therapist discusses needed modification with the orthotist by phone
Physical therapist asks the patient's consent to photograph the device and limb
Physical therapist takes photos of the device on the practice tablet
Physical therapist writes the modification request: in an e-mail today, in a short device form in the record after the change
Physical therapist checks the final request: findings, photos and the agreed change match the call with the orthotist, photos show only what is needed, and it goes to the right orthotist
Physical therapist sends the checked request and photos to the orthotist: by e-mail today, by one release through secure care messaging after the change
Physical therapist notes the device outcome in the record

tasks.design: A short device form in the practice record ({OTHER}) takes the fit findings, photos from the practice tablet and the agreed change; the therapist asks consent before photos, checks the request and releases it to the orthotist by secure care messaging, and the record keeps it with the patient's notes. Evaluating, adjusting and the call with the orthotist stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were written by hand and photos e-mailed from phones.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice records hold forms with photos and send them securely.
tasks.still_hard: Fit is judged by watching and touching; the form only records it.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing from a patient's walk that the socket rubs before they say so.

reach.learn: Whether structured requests with photos cut call-backs.

evidence.claim: Practice records hold forms with photos and send them by secure care messaging.
Photos of a patient's body are health data; sharing needs a care purpose and a secure channel.

assumptions: Boundary: from evaluating the device to the recorded outcome; making the modification is outside.
Input contract: device details from the orthotist's delivery note; form set by the practice's therapists; fallback is e-mail.
Evaluating, adjusting and calls do not change.
Orthotist time is outside the therapist's savings.

s4 keeps 80: the form saves layout and attaching, but the request is the therapist's own first write. Consent (s3b) and photos (s3c) take 1 each from the old request share. s5 keeps 10 for the release. s6 keeps 70 because the request is kept with the notes and not retyped; the outcome is still written.
research_questions: Do orthotists call back less often?

incremental.description: No new work: asking consent and taking photos are shown in s3b and s3c.

approvals.approved_version: The modification request with findings, photos and the agreed change exactly as checked by the therapist in s4b, sent once by secure care messaging to the named orthotist; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: orthotists are not on secure messaging, so s5 keeps 100, and the form saves little, so s4 keeps 95 (1.9); high: form and secure messaging as designed (6.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The physical therapist keeps teaching, judging findings, discharge and fitting; letters, reports and e-mails shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist whose letters leave the practice the same day without typing.
